title: Microsoft AI ships MAI-Transcribe-2, undercutting OpenAI and ElevenLabs on price and accuracy
subtitle: The 10-person team's new speech model tops the FLEURS benchmark across 60 languages at $0.10 per audio hour — a 72% cut from Microsoft's own prior release five months ago.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Microsoft AI on September 3 released MAI-Transcribe-2, a speech-recognition model it says ranks first on the FLEURS multilingual benchmark across 60 languages with an average 5.2% word error rate. The model adds speaker diarization, configurable transcription styles and word-level timestamps, and Microsoft says it delivers up to 10× faster inference than leading competitors on long-form audio. Pricing is $0.10 per audio hour — a 72% cut from the $0.36 that the first MAI-Transcribe model launched at five months ago.

The delta that matters is the head-to-head. Microsoft's own benchmark table shows MAI-Transcribe-2 ahead of Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, GPT-Transcribe, Whisper V3-Large and ElevenLabs's ScribeV2 across the languages tested, with the biggest accuracy gaps on non-English audio. The model was built by a 10-person team inside the Microsoft AI (MAI) group led by Mustafa Suleyman, which has been consistently shipping frontier-competitive small models — MAI-1-Preview, MAI-Voice-1, and now MAI-Transcribe-2 — while consuming a fraction of the compute of the labs it competes with.

This is the second data point in a short arc. Microsoft's MAI group is aimed squarely at the transcription and voice slice of Azure's stack, which had leaned on OpenAI Whisper and third parties. Shipping an in-house model that undercuts every incumbent by more than half on price, and beats them on the standard benchmark, is how Microsoft moves that revenue and that latency in-house — without waiting for OpenAI's roadmap or paying ElevenLabs's margins. The broader signal for the speech market is that inference costs at the frontier are collapsing faster than the pricing pages are updating.

For learners, this is the plainest kind of practical news you get in an AI feed: a real, hosted API just got dramatically cheaper and better. If you have been putting off building a transcription workflow because the cost math did not close, run it again at $0.10 an hour. And if you are learning by shipping tools, note the pattern — a ten-person team can now ship a category-leading model on a specific problem. Narrow scope is not a consolation prize; it is the leverage.
